Classes

Learn the math.

Pick the math class you’re taking, find the unit and topic you’re on in school, and practise it with mountain biking labs built for exactly that idea.

Courses

  • Algebra 1

    Explore equations, variables, functions, graphs, and linear relationships through trail gradients, speed, distance, elevation, and riding scenarios.

    • Expressions
    • Equations
    • Linear functions
    • Systems
    • Exponents
    • Quadratics
    • Statistics

    9 units · 42 topics · 1 learning activity

    Enter Algebra 1 →

  • Algebra 2

    Explore advanced algebra, quadratic functions, polynomials, exponential relationships, and mathematical modeling through jump trajectories, suspension behavior, speed, and performance data.

    • Functions
    • Quadratics
    • Polynomials
    • Rational functions
    • Logarithms
    • Sequences
    • Probability

    9 units · 42 topics · activities in development

    Enter Algebra 2 →

  • Geometry

    Explore angles, triangles, circles, transformations, area, volume, and spatial reasoning through bike design, trail construction, jump shapes, and mountain bike geometry.

    • Angles
    • Proof
    • Triangles
    • Transformations
    • Similarity
    • Circles
    • Area and volume

    9 units · 43 topics · 1 learning activity

    Enter Geometry →

  • Precalculus

    Explore advanced functions, trigonometry, periodic behavior, vectors, and mathematical modeling through jumps, trail profiles, rotational movement, and mountain biking physics.

    • Functions
    • Trigonometry
    • Periodic functions
    • Vectors
    • Parametric equations
    • Polar
    • Limits

    9 units · 41 topics · activities in development

    Enter Precalculus →

Classes follow a common US high school sequence. Your school’s order may differ: every topic is its own page, so jump straight to what you’re learning. Looking for standalone games and simulations? They’re in the Lab.
